title: Streaming sieve + drift detector to reduce downstream noise and surface schema shifts
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Problem: Console backend receives bursts of noisy, malformed, or low-value events from SDKs and downstream proxies. This noise increases compute/cost in the real-time enrichment and aggregation stages and causes false positives in usage dashboards. We also lack an automated mechanism to detect schema or distribution drift in event payloads from clients, which delays incident detection and increases backfill scope.

Goal: Implement a lightweight pre-processing layer — 'stream sieve' — deployed at the ingestion frontier that: 1) classifies events into keep/drop/low-fidelity buckets using a compact heuristic model and sampling policy, 2) performs minimal schema validation and normalization, 3) computes and emits drift indicators (per-field type/count histograms, top-k values, missing-rate deltas) to an internal drift detector microservice. The detector should surface tenants and routes with statistically significant changes and generate automated tickets/alerts and optional backfill jobs.

Scope: Build the sieve as a horizontally scalable stream processor (Rust/Go service) that sits before the enrichment queue. Provide configuration per-tenant and per-route: sampling rates, strictness level, and a grace-window. The detector will maintain sliding-window summaries (count, cardinality, median length) and compare windows using lightweight tests (ADWIN or KL divergence approximations). We will not ship model-based heavy heuristics in phase 1 to keep CPU low.

Success criteria: 1) 25-40% reduction in downstream RPS to enrichment workers for noisy routes; 2) median end-to-end ingest latency increase <5ms; 3) automated detection of schema drift within 1 hour for 90% of synthetic test cases; 4) operational dashboard showing per-route sieve decisions and drift alerts integrated into Console.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Asha: Drafted initial proposal, aligned with Observability and Ingest teams. Link to design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/stream-sieve-design (internal).

2026-02-25 - Diego: POC wireframe implemented in a branch: github.com/redwood/ingest/tree/feature/stream-sieve-poc. POC uses sampling heuristics and a counting sketch for top-k. Observed 30% RPS drop on noisy test harness.
2026-03-01 - SRE review: recommended limit on per-tenant memory and circuit breaker for high-cardinality tenants. Added pre-allocated bounded sketches and tenant-level quota enforcement.
2026-03-05 - PM review (Lina): request to emit structured drift signals to Console alerts plus a CSV export for data teams. Also asked for an opt-out toggle for enterprise customers during rollout.

2026-03-10 - Design review: decided to use an approximated KL-based change score plus missing-rate delta; defer heavy statistical tests to phase 2. Also agreed to ship with a dry-run mode that annotates events but does not drop them until metrics validate impact.
2026-03-12 - Implementation: integrated sieve as a sidecar at edge ingress. Benchmark: additional p50 latency 3.2ms, CPU per replica ~8%. Next: add config API and build Console dashboard panels.
2026-03-12 - Diego: Created PR for core sieve logic: https://github.com/redwood/ingest/pull/942 (WIP). Added unit tests for schema rules and sampling enforcement.

2026-03-12 - Ops: plan rollout as follows: 1) enable dry-run globally for 48h, 2) enable drop mode on 10% of traffic for low-risk tenants, 3) increase to 50% and monitor, 4) full enable by route after SLOs verified.
2026-03-12 - Note: related tickets ENG-111111 (hotkey fairness) and ENG-314159 (tenant-isolated-admission-control) will be consulted for quota and admission control integration.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for sieve rules, sampling and sketch correctness. 2) Integration tests with local enrichment pipeline and synthetic noise generator. 3) Load test: run test harness with 10M events/hour, assert downstream enrichment reduction and latency impact. 4) Synthetic drift scenarios (field renamed, type change, cardinality spike) to verify detector detection within 1 hour.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal dry-run (48h) with annotated events. Phase 1: selective drop on low-risk tenants (10% of tenants) and 10% traffic. Phase 2: expand to 50% after 72h of stable metrics. Phase 3: global opt-in/off in Console with per-tenant overrides. Each phase gated by dashboards (drop rate, enrich RPS, ingest latency, false-positive rate).
notes: Trade-offs: We prioritize CPU-efficient approximations over exact statistics in phase 1. This reduces detection sensitivity for rare schema changes but keeps cost predictable. If we see high false negatives, phase 2 will add more rigorous sketching and optional ML-based classification. Operational concerns: ensure data retention for sliding windows is bounded and sharded by tenant to avoid noisy neighbors.
